results.title: Authentication | Help Scout Developers
results.snippet:
This is an HTTPS-only API and it uses [OAuth 2.0 authorization](https://oauth.net/2/), implementing Authorization Code and Client Credential flows. All requests have to be authenticated via the `Authorization` header:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer f4f4994a875f461ca4d4708b9e027df4" \
https://api.helpscout.net/v2/users/me
```
The Authorization Code flow is typically used for integrations to be used by other Help Scout users. The Client Credentials flow is meant for internal integrations.
All credentials must be associated with an active, invited user in the Help Scout account; a 401 error will be returned if a user does not meet these credentials.

### OAuth2 application
You need to create an OAuth2 application before you can use the API. Create one by navigating to Your Profile > My apps and click Create My App. A redirection URL is necessary when using the **Authorization Code** flow.

This is a redirection-based flow. The application must be capable of interacting with the user-agent (i.e. the user’s web browser) and receiving API authorization codes that are routed through the user-agent.

results.title: List Conversations | Help Scout Developers
results.snippet:
# List Conversations
List and filter conversations. Use the `thread` resource link inside the Conversation entity to load conversation threads.
## Request
```
GET /v2/conversations HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer oauth_token
```
Request parameters can be used to filter conversations. All parameters are joined by the `AND` operator. If you want closed conversations in a specific inbox, call:
```
curl https://api.helpscout.net/v2/conversations?mailbox=123&status=closed
```
You can also exclude data from your search results using the `NOT` operator, calling:
```
curl https://api.helpscout.net/v2/conversations?query=(NOT email:“email@domain.com”)
```

# List Articles
- **REST Method:** GET
- **URL:** https://docsapi.helpscout.net/v1/**collections/{id}/articles**
- **URL:** https://docsapi.helpscout.net/v1/**categories/{id}/articles**
Use this endpoint to return a list of articles for a collection or category. Full articles are not returned. Instead, an [**ArticleRef**](/docs-api/objects/article-ref/) is returned, which is an abbreviated version of the Article suitable for displaying in a list.
**Note:** Articles can be listed by either a Collection or a Category.

results.title: Help Scout's AI Features: Deliver Better Support, Faster
results.snippet:
The features above bring AI into Help Scout. [Help Scout's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server](https://docs.helpscout.com/article/1779-connect-your-ai-agent-with-help-scout-to-search-conversations-and-pull-reports) does the opposite: it brings your Help Scout customer knowledge into the AI tools your team already uses.
Your help desk is one of the richest sources of customer knowledge in your entire business, but manually reviewing dozens, hundreds, or thousands of historical conversations is impractical. Help Scout's MCP server lets AI assistants like Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor securely retrieve that customer knowledge. You can use it to get information like:
- The most common questions customers ask that aren't yet covered in your knowledge base.
- Which topics or products are driving the biggest week-over-week increase in conversation volume.
- Every mention of a competitor across your conversations over the past quarter.
- The objections or hesitations prospects raise most often before purchasing.
- A summary of what a specific customer has contacted you about before your next call with them.
- The feature requests that are most frequently tied to your highest-value accounts.
